title: Why faster clearing makes access to cash a matter of minutes
summary: A clearinghouse can have enough assets to meet every obligation and still fail to deliver cash at the moment a payment falls due. Sam Schulhofer-Wohl, senior advisor to the Dallas Fed president, used that timing problem to frame his November 2 remarks to the Chicago Fed’s Financial Markets Group. A central counterparty (CCP) guarantees trades by becoming the buyer to each seller and the seller to each buyer. Netting reduces how much cash and collateral must move. Frequent margin calls protect against changes in prices and the risk of a counterparty default. Both mechanisms change where risk sits. Even if the clearinghouse reduces the probability that a failed bilateral trade disrupts the market, it must be able to collect and distribute cash to a deadline, including when a member fails.

The first question for a central bank is whether it should use a clearinghouse for its own trading. Consider a dealer that borrows in a central bank repo operation and passes funding on to another participant. If transactions on both sides can enter the same multilateral netting arrangement, the dealer may need less balance sheet to intermediate them. The relevant benefit for monetary implementation can be the effect on the dealer’s cost of passing funding into the market. The central bank’s own savings in cash or collateral offer an incomplete measure. Participation by the central bank may also encourage others to clear, increasing the set of trades available to net. The speech sets out this mechanism without quantifying either additional netting or downstream funding.

The distinction matters for the US Treasury market. As described in the speech, the Securities and Exchange Commission’s clearing requirement for covered cash transactions was due to take effect at the end of 2026, and its requirement for covered repo trades in mid-2027. Central banks were exempt and could choose whether to clear their own operations. Schulhofer-Wohl cites six central banks joining the Eurex cleared repo market, most recently the ECB. He separately identifies the Bank of Canada’s stated intention to clear repos domestically. In the US, Fed officials had discussed potential benefits. The remarks do not announce a change in where Federal Reserve operations clear or provide evidence about the effect of an implemented US change.

A second issue is what the central bank provides to the clearinghouse. Settling in central bank money reduces the credit and liquidity risks associated with the settlement asset. Access to an account and the ability to move funds at the required hour are separate constraints. In the US, a clearinghouse can hold an account at a Reserve Bank only if the Financial Stability Oversight Council designates it a systemically important financial market utility. The speech counts eight designated utilities, all designated in 2012. That count covers financial market utilities and cannot be read as eight newly eligible clearinghouses. New asset classes and trading venues could change the distribution of risks across institutions over time, while formal eligibility still turns on designation.

The payment system’s clock matters once access is in place. As of the speech, Fedwire Funds operated 22 hours per day, Monday to Friday. The Board had announced its intention to add Sundays and weekday holidays by 2028 or 2029. A further move to seven-day operation would depend on demand. Trading around the clock and instruments that expire within the day can make positions move quickly. More frequent margin collection can reduce the exposure accumulated before the next call, but collecting that margin is easier when the payment system is open. A prospective expansion of operating hours may change this timing constraint. It also leaves the clearinghouse and participants responsible for having cash available when payment is possible.

Emergency lending is a third, legally separate relationship. The clearinghouse bears primary responsibility for managing liquidity, yet a solvent institution can need funds within minutes after a default. The speech distinguishes three arrangements. UK CCPs can access the Bank of England’s operational standing facilities and discount window on the same terms as banks and broker-dealers, with repo operations excluded. The ECB has a dedicated overnight facility, which it converted in 2025 from discretionary activation to a standing tool. In the United States, lending by a Reserve Bank to a designated utility requires unusual or exigent circumstances, a majority vote of the Board after consultation with the Treasury secretary, and evidence that adequate bank credit is unavailable. A settlement account by itself provides no such lending authority. Operational readiness matters alongside legal eligibility because an approval that arrives after a payment deadline can leave serious disruption even if funding is eventually supplied.

The membership rules bring those three roles together. Some clearinghouses require members to contribute liquidity under stress. If a central bank joined in order to clear its ordinary market transactions and inherited the same obligation, decisions about emergency lending could become entangled with its contractual duties as a member. Schulhofer-Wohl raises the possibility of a distinct membership category exempt from that obligation. Its purpose would be to retain control over public lending while securing the potential netting benefits of clearing. He offers it as a design option, with no announcement of adoption. The speech expresses his views and supplies no change in the policy rate, transaction-level estimates or observed market repricing.

questions.question: Would centrally clearing Fed repo operations lower the balance-sheet cost of funding the broader market?
questions.detail: Measure the trades eligible to net with each dealer’s existing market positions, the change in gross versus net exposure and the amount of funding passed on. Compare dealers with high and low pre-existing overlap in the same clearing system. A reduction in the central bank’s settlement movements alone would miss the transmission mechanism the speaker describes.

questions.question: Which intraday liquidity constraint would longer payment hours actually relieve?
questions.detail: Compare the times of margin calls, cash receipts and settlement deadlines with payment-system operating hours, separately for ordinary days, holidays and stressed periods. Distinguish a delay caused by a closed payment system from one caused by insufficient readily available collateral or cash. The speech supplies the current operating schedule and prospective changes, while the payment records needed for such a test are separate evidence.

questions.question: Can a central bank preserve control of emergency lending while participating in ordinary clearing?
questions.detail: Assess the liquidity obligations in a clearinghouse’s membership rules alongside the authorisation and timing required for each central bank’s lending facility. Model a member default with and without a separate central-bank membership category and identify who must fund the shortfall by the deadline. The relevant outcomes include the speed of payment and the remaining obligations of other members. The speech proposes a design and provides no observed performance under it.

limitation: These are a Dallas Fed official’s personal remarks on market infrastructure. The source describes institutions and possible design changes without measuring transaction costs or announcing a policy-rate or clearing decision.
